To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
immune reconstitution disease is an increasingly recognized complication of antiretrovial treatment and that it may be associated with a wide spectrum of parasitic infections.
immune reconstitution disease associated parasitic infections are a significant problem for HIV infected patients on antiretrovirus therapy in the developing world.
IRD is a clinical syndrome that occurs in patients with HIV who have been started on ART.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1. To identify novel mechanisms of immune evasion by pathogens and how these are exploited to cause infection. 2. To identify novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of infectious disease.

the following: the clinical spectrum and the pathogenesis of IRDs associated with parasitic and mycobacterial infections; and the development of novel diagnostic tools for the detection of latent mycobacterial infections.
the development of a new class of drugs for treatment and prevention of infectious diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need to consider the possibility of IRD in patients with parasitic infection who are responding to ART.
there is an association between IRD and the following parasitic infections: leishmanias, schistosom, strongyloides, toxocara, toxoplasma, trypanosoma.
IRD is a complex clinical phenomenon that can result from a number of immunological mechanisms, including dysregulated augmentation of type 1 immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spectrum of infections associated with immune reconstitution disease is expanding to include a number of parasites, and the pathogenic mechanisms underlying these infections are different from those associated with mycobacteria, chronic viruses and invasive fungi.
immune reconstitution disease associated to parasitic infections is a clinical entity that can occur during antiretrovial treatment.
the immune reconstitution disease is associated with parasitic infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IRD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with parasitic infections, particularly in those who have recently started ART.
IRD associated with these infections is not rare.
clinicians and public health workers should have a high index of suspicion of parasitic IRD in HIV‐infected patients who are responding to ART.
